findings.observation: The Traffic Impact Analysis Determination Worksheet (supplementary document be3343ae-a570-434f-8f82-a7e396bcc27b) page 3 shows the TPW Staff Determination section. The checkbox marked with an X indicates: 'A traffic impact analysis is NOT required. No TIA report document is present in the project supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks whether a TIA report is missing when the TIA Determination indicates one is required. The determination explicitly states that a TIA is NOT required because the project does not exceed LDC thresholds. Since the condition triggering this requirement is not met (the worksheet does not indicate a TIA is required), this item is not applicable to this site plan.
findings.explanation: TIA Determination Worksheet indicates TIA is NOT required; threshold not exceeded per TPW staff determination dated 3/19/2026.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) confirmed that driveway spacing dimensions (linear distances between driveways or from driveways to intersections) are not shown on the plan. Two driveways are shown entering the site from Collier Street with callouts reading 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS', but no spacing dimensions are provided. Sheet 14 was also examined and showed no driveway spacing dimensions.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires driveway spacing dimensions to be shown on plans. The Type II Driveway detail on Sheet 30 provides construction specifications but defers spacing requirements to the Transportation Criteria Manual Section 5. The site plans show driveway locations but do not dimension the spacing between driveways or from driveways to intersections (such as the distance from the driveway to Collier/S Lamar intersection). This is a completeness deficiency.
findings.explanation: Driveway spacing dimensions not shown on site plans; two driveways on Collier Street are depicted but spacing is not dimensioned.
findings.resolution: Add dimensions showing driveway spacing on site plans: distance between the two Collier Street driveways, and distance from each driveway to the nearest street intersection.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 13 showed no driveway width dimensions at the street. Vision tool analysis of Sheet 14 confirmed curb return radii are shown with labels 'R25' at the curb returns where the proposed access drive meets Collier Street. Sheet 30 (Type II Driveway detail, Standard 433S-2) shows a dimension line labeled 'WIDTH' but Note 2 states: 'DRIVEWAY WIDTHS AND RADII DIMENSIONS; ONE/TWO WAY TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS, AND GEOMETRIC LAYOUT ARE HIGHLY VARIABLE, SUBJECT TO SITE SPECIFIC CONDITIONS AND REQUIREMENTS. SEE TRANSPORTATION CRITERIA MANUAL SECTION 5 "DRIVEWAYS".'
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires both driveway widths AND curb return radii to be shown. Curb return radii (R25) are shown on Sheet 14, which partially satisfies the requirement. However, driveway widths at the street are not dimensioned on any sheet. While the Type II Driveway standard detail exists, it explicitly defers width specifications to site-specific conditions and the TCM. For a complete submittal, the actual driveway opening widths at Collier Street should be dimensioned on the site plan.
findings.explanation: Curb return radii (R25) shown on Sheet 14, but driveway widths at street not dimensioned on site plans.
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines showing the width of each driveway opening where it intersects Collier Street.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 13 confirmed that adjacent driveways on neighboring properties are not shown on the plan. While neighboring properties along South Lamar Blvd and Collier Street are outlined and labeled (e.g., 'LOT 2 FRANK REEDER SUBDIVISION', 'LOT 12 EVERGREEN HEIGHTS', 'SOUTH LAMAR BUSINESS PARK'), no driveway curb cuts or entries are depicted on their street frontages. The validation methodology specifies looking for 'two wide, flat-bottomed U-shapes or J-shapes side by side with a gap between them', but no such features are visible on adjacent properties within the plan view.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires adjacent driveways within 300 feet to be shown on plans. This is an 'Always' requirement for all site plans. Even though the subject site has only two driveways on Collier Street, the requirement is to show neighboring driveways within 300 feet along the site's street frontages (South Lamar Blvd and Collier Street) so that TPW can evaluate driveway spacing compliance. The plan shows property boundaries but does not extend the surveyed/depicted area to include adjacent driveway locations.
findings.explanation: Adjacent driveways within 300 feet on neighboring properties are not shown on site plans; only property boundaries of adjacent parcels are depicted.
findings.resolution: Extend site plan to show and identify all existing driveways on adjacent properties within 300 feet of the subject site's driveways along South Lamar Boulevard and Collier Street.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 13 confirmed that South Lamar Boulevard appears to be an undivided street based on the visual configuration (5-lane layout with no visible raised center median or physical barrier separating opposing traffic flows). The facts.md file confirms the existing cross-section as '5U (5-lane undivided)' and future cross-section as '4D (4-lane divided, raised median)'. However, the site plan drawing cuts off at the eastern right-of-way line of South Lamar Blvd, and properties on the opposite side of the street are not depicted. Therefore, no opposing driveways are visible, and no offset dimensions to opposing driveways are shown.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item has a conditional requirement: 'If site fronts undivided street'. The site does front South Lamar Boulevard, which is currently configured as an undivided 5-lane street (5U). On undivided streets, driveway offsets from opposing driveways must be dimensioned to ensure safe operations. Since the plan does not show the opposite side of South Lamar Boulevard or any opposing driveways, it cannot demonstrate compliance with offset requirements. This is a completeness deficiency.
findings.explanation: Site fronts South Lamar Blvd (undivided 5U street), but opposing driveways across the street are not shown and offsets are not dimensioned.
findings.resolution: Extend site plan to show opposing driveways on the east side of South Lamar Boulevard and dimension the offsets from the subject site's driveways to any opposing driveways on the undivided street frontage.

findings.observation: Sheet 16 (Site Notes And Tables) contains a comprehensive parking table titled '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PARKING TABLE'. The table shows proposed land use mix with the following uses and square footages: Studio (70 units), 1 Bedroom (328 units), 2 Bedroom (55 units), 3 Bedroom (6 units), Restaurant (4,888 SF), Retail (General) (5,046 SF), and Leasing Office (5,661 SF). All land uses are clearly identified with their associated units or square footage.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires a parking table showing proposed land use(s) with square footage. Sheet 16 provides exactly this information in a clear tabular format. The table breaks down residential uses by unit type with unit counts, and commercial uses with square footage. This fully satisfies the requirement for parking calculation purposes.
findings.explanation: Parking table on Sheet 16 shows all proposed land uses (residential by unit type, commercial by SF) with complete breakdown of units/square footage.

findings.observation: Sheet 16 parking table shows 'TOTAL PRIVATE PARKING SPACES PROVIDED: 647' for vehicle parking. The table includes a detailed breakdown showing Standard (500), Compact (57), EV Ready (31), EV Capable (10), and various ADA space types totaling 26 accessible spaces, with 23 spaces labeled as 'COLLIER PUBLIC PARALLEL PARKING'. For bicycle parking, the table shows 'BICYCLE PARKING' section with columns for 'REQUIRED' (Long Term: 33-46, Short Term: 20-33) and 'PROVIDED' (Long Term: 16). Sheet 37 also shows a 'RESIDENT PARKING PROVIDED PER LEVEL' table with a total of 603 parking stalls.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires the total number of provided parking spaces (vehicle and bicycle) to be shown. Sheet 16 clearly displays total vehicle parking (647 private spaces) and bicycle parking provisions (16 long-term spaces provided). There is a minor discrepancy between the Sheet 16 total (647) and the Sheet 37 per-level total (603), but the overall requirement to show total parking numbers is met. The difference may be due to the 23 public parallel parking spaces on Collier Street and additional retail/visitor spaces.
findings.explanation: Total parking spaces shown on Sheet 16: 647 vehicle spaces (broken down by type) and bicycle parking (16 long-term provided); Sheet 37 shows 603 garage spaces by level.

findings.observation: Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) contains a 'SYMBOL LEGEND' section showing parking space dimensions: Regular Parking Space (9'-0" x 17'-0"), Compact Parking Space (7'-6" x 16'-0"), HC Accessible Parking Space (8'-0" x 18'-0" w/ 5'-0" aisle), Van Accessible Parking Space (16'-0" x 18'-0" w/ 5'-0" aisle). The legend includes diagrams showing the stall depth (18'-0" TYP for accessible and regular, 16'-0" TYP (MIN.) for compact) and width dimensions. Similar legends are present on other parking level sheets (38, 39, 40, 41).
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires parking stall width, depth, and angle to be dimensioned. Sheet 37 and other parking garage sheets provide complete dimensions for width and depth of all parking space types. While the legend does not explicitly state angles, the parking space symbols on the floor plans show 90-degree (perpendicular) parking configuration, which is the standard and can be inferred from the plan layout. The dimensional information provided is sufficient for a completeness check.
findings.explanation: Parking stall dimensions shown on Sheet 37 legend and other garage level sheets: widths (7'-6" to 16'-0") and depths (16'-0" to 18'-0") for all space types; 90-degree angle evident from plan layout.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) confirmed that parking aisle widths and internal driveway widths are not dimensioned on the parking garage plans. While the parking space dimensions are clearly shown in the legend (widths and depths), the circulation aisles where vehicles drive between rows of parking spaces have no dimension lines or annotations indicating their width. Semantic search for 'parking aisle width dimension garage circulation' returned results showing accessible parking aisle dimensions (5'-0" for HC, 8'-0" for Van accessible) which are pedestrian access aisles, not vehicular driving aisles.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires parking aisle widths or internal driveway widths to be dimensioned. The parking garage floor plans (Sheets 37-41) show the layout and parking space dimensions but lack dimensions for the vehicular circulation aisles. While the accessible parking details show pedestrian access aisle widths (5'-0" per ADA), these are not the same as the vehicular driving aisle widths needed between parking rows. This dimensional information is critical for TPW to verify adequate circulation and is a completeness deficiency.
findings.explanation: Parking aisle widths and internal driveway widths not dimensioned on parking garage plans (Sheets 37-41); only parking space dimensions shown, not circulation aisle widths.
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines on parking garage plans showing the width of vehicular circulation aisles between parking space rows and internal driveway widths for all parking levels.

findings.observation: Sheet 16 parking table provides a complete breakdown of parking spaces by type: Standard (500), Compact (57), EV Ready (31), EV Capable (10), and ADA spaces broken down as Garage Standard (10), Garage Van (2), Standard Van (1), with additional accessible space designations. Sheet 37 parking garage legend clearly identifies parking space types with symbols: R (Regular), C (Compact), HC (Accessible), VAN (Van Accessible), R-EVR (EV Charging Ready), R-EV (EV Charging Installed), HC-EV (Accessible EV), with each type labeled on the floor plans. Bicycle parking is also identified (16 long-term provided).
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires parking spaces to be identified by type (standard, compact, handicapped, bicycle). The site plan provides comprehensive identification of all parking space types through both the parking table (Sheet 16) with numerical breakdowns and the parking garage plans (Sheets 37-41) with clear symbols and legends for each type. All four required categories (standard, compact, handicapped, bicycle) are explicitly identified.
findings.explanation: Parking spaces identified by type on Sheet 16 table and Sheets 37-41 floor plans: standard (500), compact (57), handicapped/accessible (26 total with van accessible), bicycle (16 long-term), plus EV designations.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 Of 2) confirmed that accessible routes of travel are shown. The Legend includes a line type for 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' (represented by a dashed line with small circles/dots), and this line type is visible on the plan tracing the proposed sidewalks alongside the internal curved roadway/drive aisle. The accessible route connects from the public sidewalk on Collier Street into the site and along pedestrian paths.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires an accessible route of travel to be shown connecting all accessible elements. Sheet 14 clearly indicates proposed ADA paths with a distinct line type in the legend and depicts these paths on the plan. While the full connectivity to all accessible elements (parking, entries, amenities) would need to be verified across multiple sheets, the presence of designated ADA paths on the dimensional control plan satisfies the completeness requirement for showing accessible routes.
findings.explanation: Accessible route of travel shown on Sheet 14 with 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' designation in legend, depicted along internal sidewalks and connecting from Collier Street.

findings.observation: Vision tool analysis of Sheet 14 confirmed that ADA ramps are indicated on the plan. The 'KEY NOTES' section lists note number 12 as 'PROPOSED ADA RAMP', and callout symbols (circles with the number 12 inside) are visible at several locations on the plan where pedestrian paths intersect with vehicular drives, particularly near the entrance on Collier Street and at crosswalks along the internal drive. Sheet 30 also shows a Type 1B Sidewalk Curb Ramp detail (Standard 432S-5B).
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires ramps connecting accessible elements to be shown on plans. Sheet 14 uses a keynote system to identify proposed ADA ramp locations with specific callout symbols placed on the plan. The presence of these callouts at pedestrian crossing locations demonstrates that ramps are documented. Sheet 30 provides the construction detail for the ramp type. This satisfies the completeness requirement for showing ramp locations.
findings.explanation: Ramps shown on Sheet 14 with 'PROPOSED ADA RAMP' key note (#12) and callout symbols at pedestrian crossing locations; detail on Sheet 30.

findings.observation: Semantic search for 'off-site parking remote parking separate parcel walking distance' returned results related to on-site parking tables, garage parking symbols, and parking space details, but found no evidence of off-site parking proposals. Sheet 16 parking table shows all parking is provided as 'TOTAL PRIVATE PARKING SPACES PROVIDED: 647' with a breakdown showing garage parking. The table includes a column labeled 'COLLIER PUBLIC PARALLEL PARKING' showing 23 spaces, but these appear to be public street parking spaces on Collier Street (within the public right-of-way), not off-site parking on a separate parcel per LDC 25-6-501. No supplementary documents or site plan sheets describe off-site parking arrangements, agreements, or locations on separate properties.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item has a conditional requirement: 'If proposing off-site parking'. Off-site parking per LDC 25-6-501 refers to parking provided on a separate parcel to meet the subject site's parking requirements, typically requiring recorded access agreements and specific dimensional compliance. The Collier Street parallel parking appears to be public on-street parking, not off-site parking meeting LDC 25-6-501 requirements. Since there is no evidence of off-site parking being proposed to meet parking requirements, this item is not applicable.
findings.explanation: No off-site parking proposed; all required parking provided on-site (647 private spaces in garage); public street parking on Collier Street is not off-site parking per LDC 25-6-501.

findings.observation: As documented in OSP-01, semantic search and review of all parking-related documents (Sheet 16 parking table, Sheets 37-41 parking garage plans, and supplementary documents) found no evidence of off-site parking being proposed. All parking to meet the project's requirements is provided on-site within the building's parking garage structure. The parking table shows 647 private parking spaces, all of which are located within the subject property. No walking distance dimensions from off-site parking facilities to the use served are shown because no off-site parking is proposed.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item has a conditional requirement: 'If proposing off-site parking'. Since the project does not propose off-site parking per LDC 25-6-501 (all required parking is on-site), the requirement to show walking distances between off-site parking and the use served does not apply. This item is not applicable to this site plan submission.
findings.explanation: No off-site parking proposed; all parking on-site, therefore no walking distance dimensions to off-site parking are required or expected.

summary: 8 of 14 items pass, 5 items fail, 3 items not-applicable. Failures: driveway spacing dimensions, driveway widths, adjacent driveways within 300 feet not shown, opposing driveway offsets on undivided street, and parking aisle widths not dimensioned.
